[[File:Randycarlyle 2006nhlawards.jpg|thumb|right|Randy Carlyle is the winningest coach in franchise history; in two combined tenures, he went 384–256–96 as coach.]]
The [[Anaheim Ducks]] are a professional [[ice hockey]] team based in [[Anaheim, California]]. They play in the [[Pacific Division (NHL)|Pacific Division]] of the [[Western Conference (NHL)|Western Conference]] in the [[National Hockey League]] (NHL).<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nhl.com/ice/teams.htm|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090311030113/http://www.nhl.com/ice/teams.htm|url-status=dead|archive-date=March 11, 2009|title=Teams|publisher=National Hockey League|work= NHL.com|access-date=February 6, 2009}}</ref> The franchise was founded in 1993 by [[The Walt Disney Company]] as the Mighty Ducks of Anaheim, based on the film [[The Mighty Ducks (film)|The Mighty Ducks]]. They were then renamed the Anaheim Ducks before the [[2006–07 NHL season|2006–07 season]], in which the Ducks won their first [[List of Stanley Cup champions|Stanley Cup championship]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://ducks.nhl.com/team/app/?service=page&page=NHLPage&id=16478|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071012094325/http://ducks.nhl.com/team/app/?service=page&page=NHLPage&id=16478|url-status=dead|archive-date=October 12, 2007|title=The Ducks Look|publisher=National Hockey League|work=NHL.com|access-date=February 6, 2009}}</ref><ref name="Cup" /> The Ducks have played their home games at the [[Honda Center]], formerly known as the Anaheim Arena (1993) and the Arrowhead Pond of Anaheim (1993–2006), since their inaugural season.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.hondacenter.com/Factsheet.aspx|title=Honda Center Fact Sheet|publisher=[[Honda Center]]|access-date=February 6, 2009|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081218131219/http://www.hondacenter.com/Factsheet.aspx|archive-date=December 18, 2008}}</ref> The team is owned by [[Henry Samueli]] and his wife Susan, [[Pat Verbeek]] is the [[general manager]],<ref>{{cite web|title=Executive management & hockey operations|url=https://www.nhl.com/ducks/team/hockey-operations-staff|website=NHL.com|access-date=May 15, 2026}}</ref> and [[Radko Gudas]] is the team [[Captain (ice hockey)|captain]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Radko Gudas named Ducks' first captain since Getzlaf|url=https://www.espn.com/nhl/story/_/id/41329150/radko-gudas-named-ducks-first-captain-getzlaf|website=ESPN.com|access-date=May 15, 2026|date=September 19, 2024}}</ref>

There have been 12 [[head coach]]es in franchise history. The Mighty Ducks' first head coach was [[Ron Wilson (ice hockey b. 1955)|Ron Wilson]], who coached for four seasons. [[Randy Carlyle]] is the franchise's all-time leader in regular season for most games coached, wins, [[Point (ice hockey)|points]], and also in playoff games coached and wins. Carlyle is the only head coach to have won the [[Stanley Cup]]. Carlyle was relieved of his coaching duties in on November 30, 2011, and the franchise immediately hired former [[Washington Capitals]] coach [[Bruce Boudreau]]. Boudreau was released after the 2015–16 season. The franchise rehired Carlyle prior to the 2016–17 season, for his second stint with the organization. After struggling to win games in the 2018–19 season, Carlyle was relieved on February 10, 2019. Franchise's general manager, [[Bob Murray (ice hockey, born 1954)|Bob Murray]], replaced Carlyle as interim coach to finish the 2018–19 season. After the conclusion of the season, [[Dallas Eakins]] was hired on June 17, 2019, and served as head coach until April 14, 2023, when his contract was not renewed. [[Greg Cronin]] was hired on June 5, 2023, to replace Eakins,<ref>{{cite web|title=Ducks Name Greg Cronin Head Coach|url=https://www.nhl.com/ducks/news/ducks-name-greg-cronin-head-coach-344732768|website=NHL.com|access-date=June 5, 2023|date=June 5, 2023}}</ref> served two seasons as head coach, before he was fired on April 19, 2025.<ref>{{cite web|last=Stephens|first=Eric|url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/6292123/2025/04/19/ducks-fire-coach-greg-cronin/|title=Anaheim Ducks fire coach Greg Cronin after 2 seasons|work=[[The Athletic]]|date=April 19, 2025|access-date=April 19, 2025}}</ref>

The current head coach is [[Joel Quenneville]] who was hired on May 8, 2025.<ref>{{cite web|title=Ducks hire Joel Quenneville as head coach after reinstatement following abuse scandal|url=https://www.sportsnet.ca/nhl/article/ducks-expected-to-hire-joel-quenneville-as-head-coach/|website=Sportsnet.ca|access-date=May 15, 2026|date=May 8, 2025}}</ref>
